clues: This small town sits in Portugal. It lies by a bay, with the sea close at hand.
Strong winds come from the north here, but a small range of hills blocks them. So the beach stays calm and snug.
In the 1600s, pirates kept raiding this town, so the people built a long wall to keep them out. It still stands today.
This is a true fishing town, not just a beach stop for guests. Many of its people still catch fish for a living today.
One long beach runs along the front of this town. Bars and seafood spots look out over the bay beside it.
